newsitem.title: USA: Surplus soil moisture delays plantings in Arkansas.
newsitem.headline: Surplus soil moisture delays plantings in Arkansas.

text.p: Surplus soil moisture delayed crop planting in most counties during the week ended April 13, according to state's Agricultural Statistics Service latest crop report.
Corn, rice and sorghum planting progressed in some counties, while other farmers prepared their fields for planting, the report said.
Three days were suitable for fieldwork, the report said.
Corn was 62 percent planted versus 53 a year ago and the 56 five-year average.
Rice was eight percent planted versus eight a year ago and the 14 percent average.
Sorghum was 21 percent planted 12 a year ago and 14 for the five-year average.
Winter wheat was 26 percent headed versus 14 a year ago and the eight percent average. The crop was rated seven percent excellent, 28 percent good, 45 fair, 17 poor and three very poor.
Oats were rated six percent good, 83 fair, and 11 percent poor.
Soil moisture was rated 55 percent surplus and 45 percent adequate.
